report_title: WiFi Sentinel V2.0 - Offensive Security Assessment
Executive Summary: Assessment completed with 6 reported security finding(s). Finding severity and confidence reflect the supplied evidence.

Security Findings.title: Exposed network service: msrpc
Security Findings.description: Enumeration reported this service as open from the scan vantage point. The results do not establish whether it is necessary or appropriately restricted.
Security Findings.attack_scenario: An authorized tester could verify that the service is intended to be reachable from this network segment and review its access controls.
Security Findings.impact: An exposed service increases the reachable network surface; impact depends on its purpose, configuration, and access controls.
Security Findings.remediation: Confirm the service is required, restrict it to trusted sources, and disable it if it is not needed.
evidence: Enumeration reported TCP port 135 as open.
references: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, Control 4: Secure Configuration of Enterprise Assets and Software

Security Findings.title: Service identification is incomplete
Security Findings.description: Enumeration did not provide a complete service, product, and version identification. No vulnerability is inferred from this gap.
Security Findings.attack_scenario: An authorized tester could use approved, non-invasive identification methods to confirm the asset inventory and determine relevant vendor advisories.
Security Findings.impact: Incomplete identification can make patch and exposure reviews less reliable.
Security Findings.remediation: Confirm the service owner and software identity through approved inventory or safe identification methods, then keep the software inventory current.
evidence: Enumeration reported TCP port 135 as open.
references: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, Control 2: Inventory and Control of Software Assets
